newsitem.title: FINLAND: ROLE OF FINNISH FISCAL POLICY TO GROW WHEN IN EMU.
newsitem.headline: ROLE OF FINNISH FISCAL POLICY TO GROW WHEN IN EMU.

text.p: The role of fiscal policy will grow if Finland enters the third stage of European economic and monetary union (EMU) and loses its monetary policy independence, economics professor Jukka Pekkarinen said on Friday.

Addressing a seminar, Pekkarinen -- chairman of an expert group appointed by Prime Minister Paavo Lipponen to review the pros and cons of Finnish EMU membership -- did not voice any opinion for or against participation as he outlined the potential effects of Finland joining the single currency.
Following are highlights from his presentation:
* "The role of fiscal (budget) policy will accentuate when there is no independent monetary policy."

* "Although EMU will bring monetary stability, moderate inflation and real interest rates -- there are risks in giving up the autonomy of national monetary policy. The conditions of a peripheral country differ from the European core."
* "The surplus from employment pension funds will give buffers against cyclical changes during normal conditions."
* "But buffer funds could be created to collect for example social- and unemployment security funds to help through the cyclical changes."
* "When looking at the labour markets, I stress the importance of adjusting to (living with) moderate inflation. A rising wage trend is a big risk in an EMU environment."
* "An open question is how much should flexibility of nominal wages be increased (in EMU)."
* "It would be desirable to have both Sweden and England joining EMU in the first wave."
* "There will be non-recurring costs from the (EMU) project but the gains and advantages are permanent."
